name: Bücker Bü 131 Jungmann / CASA 1.131
summary: Compact German 1930s trainer biplane that is also a favourite sport aerobatic type; licence-built in Spain, Czechoslovakia, Switzerland and elsewhere.

wings: Swept-back, staggered biplane wings of near-equal span
Ailerons on both upper and lower wings
engines: Inverted inline four-cylinder Hirth or Tigre engine with a neat metal-covered nose
fuselage: Metal-covered front fuselage with fabric aft

tellTales: Compact swept-wing biplane with ailerons on all four wing panels
Neat inline-engine nose with two tandem open cockpits

confusedWith.howToTell: The Tiger Moth has lower-wing ailerons only; the Jungmann has ailerons on both upper and lower wings and a stubbier, smoother nose.
The Jungmann has visibly swept-back wings; the Stampe wings look straighter with little sweep.
The Stearman is much larger with a radial engine; the Jungmann is a small, light inline-engine biplane.
